title: Does routine compression undo LLM unlearning? A short project
primary_claim: Standard post-training compression (quantization, magnitude pruning, SVD truncation) mostly does not reverse unlearning on TOFU forget10 / Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct across NPO, SimNPO, and IdkDPO unlearning methods, but the strongest reversal came from magnitude pruning in a narrow 10-20% sparsity window on NPO unlearning, recovering up to 42% of the ceiling-baseline gap.
target_value: 4-bit quantization on NPO: 22% recovery; magnitude pruning at 20% sparsity on NPO: 42% recovery peak; SVD truncation: no significant recovery (-26% at 99% keep); SimNPO/IdkDPO: <=3% recovery in all non-destructive cells

title:
Compositionality and Ambiguity: 
Latent Co-occurrence and Interpretable Subspaces
primary_claim: SAE latents are not always independent: a small fraction of latents in GPT2-Small and Gemma-2-2b (Gemma Scope) SAEs form co-occurrence clusters that map interpretable subspaces, including cases of compositional encoding (e.g. discrete quantifiers like 'one of'/'some of'/'all of' combine predictably by relative activation strength) and cases where co-occurrence reflects lexical ambiguity (e.g. senses of 'how'); the rate of co-occurrence and the size/prevalence of these clusters both decrease as SAE width increases.
metric: rate of SAE latent co-occurrence per token vs SAE width
target_value: co-occurrence rate decreases monotonically as SAE width increases in both GPT2-Small (widths 768-49152) and Gemma-2-2b; cluster (subgraph) size and prevalence also decrease as SAE width increases

title: Exploring Generalization in NLA's
primary_claim: A Natural Language Autoencoder's Activation Verbalizer trained only at layer 20 of Qwen2.5-7B generalizes without retraining to reconstruct activations from layers 10-25, beating both a random-noise baseline and a shuffled-correspondence baseline on cosine similarity, Recall@10, FVE, and nRMSE, while early layers (0-1) and late layer 27 fail to generalize.
metric: cosine similarity / Recall@10 / FVE / nRMSE for layer-20-trained AV reconstructing activations across layers, vs random and shuffled baselines
target_value: cosine similarity >0.50 and Recall@10 >0.40 from L10-L25; every layer significant vs random baseline (Wilcoxon signed-rank + Benjamini-Hochberg); L0, L1, L27 fail against the shuffled baseline

title: Eval-Awareness Steering detects the Test, Not the Sabotage
primary_claim: In Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the internal difference-of-means 'eval-awareness' direction is a genuine detector of evaluation framing (~0.81 AUROC on novel format-matched framings) but steering with it does not causally drive sandbagging (flat dose-response that fails to beat an empirical null of 24 random directions) nor predict which individual items get sandbagged (per-item probe AUROC ~0.54, at chance).
metric: swing in sandbagging accuracy from steering dose alpha=-2 to alpha=+2 at headline layer 12, vs empirical null of 24 random directions
target_value: -1.77pp swing, sub-threshold Spearman rho=-0.53 (p=0.08), does not beat empirical null (p=0.20)

title: A necessity check for linear safety probes
primary_claim: Linear safety probes that successfully detect (AUROC≥0.91) and steer a feature often fail to 'silence' it via causal projection, showing that detect/steer success is not evidence of a true causal handle; a calibration-time cosine diagnostic between plain and within-class-whitened difference-of-means directions predicts silencing success across 4-5 model families and 2 features, recovering all 17 existing causal handles and correctly alarming on the remaining 5 in a 22-cell battery.
metric: necessity-check protocol recovery of true causal handles vs. correct alarms, 22-cell battery
target_value: recovers all 17 causal handles that exist and correctly alarms on the remaining 5

title: Tracing Typos in LLMs: My Attempt at Understanding How Models Correct Misspellings
primary_claim: A single attention head (L0H3) in Llama-3.2-1B, a 'subword merging head' that moves information between subword tokens of the same word, is the primary component responsible for typo correction when no surrounding context is available; ablating it breaks typo correction (measured via logit difference) while leaving normal text and general MLP-driven performance unaffected.
metric: logit difference change upon single-head ablation
target_value: only the subword merging head (L0H3) showed a significant impact on logit difference when ablated one-by-one across all attention heads

title: The Self-Hating Attention Head: A Deep Dive in GPT-2
primary_claim: GPT2-small's attention head L1H5 attends to semantically similar tokens while actively suppressing self-attention, a mechanism driven by negative eigenvalues in the symmetric part of its QK circuit, and this self-suppression can be causally steered by scaling those negative eigenvalues.
metric: negative eigenvalues in the symmetric QK matrix W_sym

title: MHC Interp #1: Previous-Token Heads Become Attention Sinks Under Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
primary_claim: In small (781M-parameter) models trained with Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), previous-token attention heads change character and become attention-sink-like with high kurtosis signatures instead of showing the canonical previous-token diagonal-stripe pattern, while induction heads remain detectable by the standard pattern in both mHC and non-mHC models.
metric: layer-of-90%-final-top-1-accuracy (logit lens), attention head detection agreement
target_value: mHC reaches 90% of final top-1 accuracy by layer 22 vs residual L31 and mhc-lite L35; KL(lens||final) < 0.5 by L24 in mHC vs L34 in residual; all converge to ~38.2% top-1 at L35
